title: From the Internet of Things to Physical AI: What Really Changed?
style: Black-and-white engraved editorial illustration inspired by mid-20th-century popular-science printmaking

images.alt: The evolution of manufacturing, from manually operated lathes to CNC automation and robotic production.
images.caption: From manual lathes and mechanization to numerical control and robot-assisted manufacturing.

images.alt: Diagram showing a text command, LLM, RAG retrieval, navigation, sensors, and feedback.
images.caption: The language model interprets the instruction, retrieves knowledge through RAG, and passes a navigation goal to the robot without controlling its motors directly.

images.alt: Engraved illustrative RViz2 map with Alpha, Beta, and Gamma and a planned route to Beta.
images.caption: Conceptual reconstruction of the experiment: the RAG knowledge base held coordinates mapped to the names Alpha, Beta, and Gamma. A free-form text command could request a destination by name, and the model passed its coordinates to the navigation system.

images.alt: A robot with cameras and an air-sampling sensor leans gently toward a lily.
images.caption: Can machines learn about the physical world through their own interactions? An editorial illustration, not a depiction of a deployed system.

editorial_note: The RViz2 image is an artistic reconstruction, not an actual application screenshot. Coordinates are illustrative.
